title: Los Angeles restaurant takeover: separate ownership, menu changes and plan review
description: The county food permit and the city premises decisions belong in different parts of the opening file.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Buying the fitted restaurant does not transfer its health permission
paragraphs: The county’s permit form ties the record to the actual person, location, activity and period, and states that it is not transferable. Its purchase instructions direct an existing-restaurant buyer without anticipated major permitted construction to the relevant district office. That route is not a promise that the previous owner’s permission carries over.

List the proposed menu, equipment and operating-method changes separately. The application terms call for review and approval of such changes; a purchase described as unchanged may still alter the food process.

sections.heading: A changed layout or cooking process creates a plan file
paragraphs: The plan-check page identifies new facilities, previously unpermitted food spaces and specified remodel/equipment changes. It calls for a scaled plan package, actual menu and equipment information, alongside separate planning/building and health decisions. Track required construction approvals, inspections and issued permit rather than using the application date as the opening date.

For a City of Los Angeles address, confirm the city’s premises authority and the county’s food-health role. The county program expressly excludes Pasadena, Long Beach and Vernon; a Los Angeles-area mailing label is insufficient.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the new owner adds cooking equipment
paragraphs: A buyer plans to keep a small restaurant’s dining area but add a fryer and change the menu. Before fixing a launch date, its operations lead compares the prior records with the new menu/equipment and obtains the applicable county review path. Its premises lead tracks city approvals separately. The lease and equipment purchase are commercial commitments, not those agency decisions.

sections.heading: Keep the purchase and opening records connected

rows: Operator
Actual owner, address, service jurisdiction and prior facility records
Food/process lead
Proposed menu, method, equipment and applicable review route
Designer/premises lead
Required plans, city permits and construction approvals
Opening lead
Applicable inspection/conditional approval and issued health permit
Finance
Separate invoiced review/permit and fit-out costs; unresolved amounts remain unknown

sections.heading: Keep this restaurant question narrow
paragraphs: No actual site, exemption, fee, expedited review deadline or technical design is approved here. Alcohol, outdoor use, fire, grease discharge, accessibility, food-worker obligations and city business-tax registration remain separate. The current application form is marked 12/3/25; confirm the latest required documents for the actual filing.

practicalOutput: A City of Los Angeles restaurant purchase/change matrix separating the actual owner, county food review, city premises approvals and issued opening evidence.
limitations: Defined county food-permit/process branch for a City of Los Angeles site; not all restaurant or county-city requirements.
Actual address, technical process, alcohol/fire/grease/accessibility, workforce, fees and current filing requirements remain unresolved.

title: Houston laundry wastewater: check the process before claiming a permit exception
description: The city’s non-industrial laundry distinction does not settle every discharge or survey obligation.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Commercial and industrial laundry are not interchangeable labels
paragraphs: Houston Public Works lists self-service or commercial, expressly not industrial, laundry outside the stated Industrial Waste Permit requirement. The same FAQ reserves a permit determination where a facility discharges industrial waste. Do not turn that qualified distinction into an assurance that every laundry can discharge without conditions.

First identify the actual receiving sewer authority, clients, textiles, contamination, chemicals and processing. A Houston postal address or a brochure calling the plant commercial does not establish the city sewer jurisdiction or discharge classification.

For a proposed non-domestic discharge to the city sewer, the FAQ directs the facility to contact IWS and complete/submit its survey for review and next steps. Follow that prospective-discharge route independently of whether a survey arrives in the mail.

sections.heading: A survey request is a separate evidence task
paragraphs: The city describes a received Industrial Wastewater Survey as a mandatory report request. Its guidance distinguishes process water, washdown, boiler and other water uses, and batch from continuous discharge. Assign the actual due date, signer and operational data.
Retain the response and IWS follow-up. Neither sending the survey nor receiving an invoice is an issued permit or an answer to all discharge restrictions.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the linen plant expands its customer mix
paragraphs: A laundry partner proposes a new plant and a second customer segment. Its engineer documents the actual textiles/processes and receiving system before relying on the non-industrial category. Its manager separately answers a received survey and records the IWS determination. Equipment orders and the launch budget wait for that evidence and the separate premises decisions.

rows: Operator
Actual site, clients, textiles and service process
Engineer
Receiving authority, water uses, chemicals, flow and discharge pattern
Response owner
Prospective IWS survey; any received request, due date and signed response
Permit lead
IWS determination and applicable issued/control evidence
Premises/finance
Separate occupancy, utilities, treatment and unresolved cost records

sections.heading: What this does not establish
paragraphs: No real plant is classified, no treatment system is designed and no numeric pollutant limit or fee is supplied. Prohibited discharges, actual limits, state/federal categories, stormwater/direct discharge, boilers, fire/building, workers and Houston occupancy requirements require their own evidence.

practicalOutput: A Houston laundry process/receiving-authority and prospective-survey file, with the actual IWS determination and any received-notice response recorded separately.
limitations: Houston sanitary-sewer guidance only; no actual laundry classification, blanket permit exemption or unrestricted discharge.
Actual receiving jurisdiction, water/process/flow facts, limits, treatment, premises, state/federal overlays and costs remain unresolved.
